collection.title: Central California Migrant Camp Voices, 1940–1941
collection.source_collection: Voices from the Dust Bowl: The Charles L. Todd and Robert Sonkin Migrant Worker Collection, 1940 to 1941
collection.repository: American Folklife Center, Library of Congress
collection.introduction: Between 1940 and 1941, Charles L. Todd and Robert Sonkin recorded conversations, meetings, stories, songs, and daily experience in Farm Security Administration migrant worker camps across central California. This bounded selection follows four voices and public moments across Shafter, El Rio, Visalia, and Yuba City.
collection.interpretive_note: These recordings preserve individual testimony and community activity within a larger federal collecting project. Present the people represented as historical participants, not as visual atmosphere. Keep names, places, dates, source notes, and credit lines attached to their records.
collection.rights_note: The Library of Congress states that it is not aware of U.S. copyright protection or other restrictions in this collection except as noted, while reminding users that privacy, publicity, cultural sensitivity, and item-specific rights may still apply. Every displayed item must retain its Library of Congress source link and credit line.
collection.credit_line: Charles L. Todd and Robert Sonkin migrant workers collection (AFC 1985/001), American Folklife Center, Library of Congress

records.title: Interview about dust storms in Oklahoma

records.title: Interview about the camp closing, discrimination, labor issues, efforts to organize youth, citizenship
records.summary: Augustus Martinez discusses the closing of the El Rio camp, discrimination, labor issues, efforts to organize youth, and citizenship. The Library of Congress notes that he was thirty at the time and had come to the United States from Mexico at age nine.
records.short_summary: Camp closure, discrimination, labor, youth organizing, and citizenship in El Rio.
